label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
Last Saturday, our student-run Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms (5–7 November 2026, Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune) came to a close. I was one of the three organisers, along with Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza, and this is my thank-you note on behalf of the team.

We received 112 applications for 41 seats. Participants were MSc and early PhD students from nine states, selected on the basis of a statement and one reference. The event was supported by an institute student initiative grant of Rs 2.4 lakh, which covered hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students. It was not a picnic: three days of lectures, problem sessions and discussions, and the room was still full on the last afternoon.

Thank you to our speakers: Dr Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad), who introduced the Mordell–Weil theorem; Dr Sunanda Iyer (Chennai), who took us through modular forms; and Dr Tomasz Wierzbicki (Kraków), who joined online for computations in Sage. Sunanda ma'am, one more thank you for taking the correction so gracefully. An MSc student from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in her notes; she corrected it live and thanked him. That moment said a lot about the atmosphere we wanted.

Thank you to Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, our faculty mentor, for steady guidance before and during the school. Thank you to Mr Prakash Salunke from the office, who sorted out hostel rooms at 11pm when our booking went wrong. Thank you to the six PhD students who did TA work and ran the problem sessions. That format worked very well, and we plan to keep it.

The Day 2 power cut deserves a mention. Nearly two hours without power, laptops dying, and we moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards. It ended up being the best session of the three days.

Small schools like this matter, perhaps more than big conferences do for MSc students. They get to ask questions, make mistakes and be taken seriously.

Slides and problem sheets will be posted on the department website within two weeks. We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, subject to funding. Thank you to all the participants, and to everyone who made this one possible.
